title: Odd covers for complete graphs and complete 3-graphs
summary: The Graham-Pollak theorem says that one needs at least $n - 1$ complete bipartite graphs to cover each edge of a complete graph $K_{n}$ on $n$ vertices exactly once. The odd cover problem is a parity analogue which seeks the minimum number of complete bipartite graphs, denoted by $b_2(n)$, such that each edge of $ K_n $ is covered an odd number of times. An odd cover of a complte 3-graph $K_n^{(3)}$ on $n$ vertices is a family of complete $3$-partite $3$-graphs such that every triple is covered an odd number of times.
